title: The Shift to Agentic AI: Redefining Compute, Enterprise, and the Future of Physical Intelligence
description: This discussion explores the accelerating shift toward agentic AI, emphasizing that compute infrastructure must evolve beyond traditional GPUs to include CPUs, focusing on building open, distributed platforms for enterprise deployment and the eventual realization of physical AI.
summary:
The discussion opened by highlighting the incredible pace of AI progress, noting the transition from simple chatbots to complex, goal-oriented agentic AI systems. This shift has created an unprecedented demand for compute, requiring not only powerful GPUs but also increased CPU infrastructure for orchestration.

The speakers emphasized a multi-faceted strategy centered on building open platforms and a robust ecosystem. Anthropik and OpenAI discussed how open platforms enable models to scale across various partners, while AMD introduced Venus, a new infrastructure designed to handle agentic AI workloads by leveraging the strengths of x86 architecture alongside GPUs. This highlights that the role of the CPU is becoming increasingly critical in a world where agents run distributed systems.

Furthermore, the discussion addressed the evolving requirements for enterprise AI, focusing on distributed deployment models that combine frontier models, cloud services, and on-prem infrastructure. Enterprise AI adoption is now driven by specific use cases like autonomous threat detection and personalized AI assistants running locally, requiring robust security and management.

The conversation culminated in the vision of Physical AI, where agents move beyond digital answers to take real-world actions. AMD introduced the Crea AI system, designed to unify CPU, GPU, and NPU capabilities into a single module to power real-time perception and reasoning. title: The Accelerated Scaling of AI Compute: From Training to Inference and the Future of AI Hardware
description: This discussion outlines the explosive growth in AI compute demand, shifting focus from training to inference, and details the massive market projections for AI accelerators. The speaker highlights the critical role of CPUs and AMD in this landscape, along with the strategic roadmap for future AI architecture.
summary:
The transcript details the rapidly accelerating scaling of AI compute, noting that training flops increase by 5x annually and monthly token consumption is skyrocketing, creating immense demand for compute resources. A major shift is the growth of AI inference, with projections suggesting that 60% of global AI compute capacity will be used for inference by 2026. This demand is projected to drive the AI accelerator market to $1.4 trillion by 2030, approaching the size of the entire semiconductor market.

The speaker emphasizes that scaling is achieved by combining better compute with better models, driving down the cost per token for enterprises through optimized hardware like the 350P chip and intelligent routing. A significant focus is placed on CPUs, noting that the server CPU market is expected to grow substantially, and highlighting AMD's strong position, with a large percentage of Fortune 100 companies adopting Epic.

Looking ahead, the speaker outlines a clear roadmap for future AI hardware, introducing Florence as the next-generation CPU and Ravenna as the eighth generation of the Epic family. This strategy aims to provide customers with a predictable and scalable infrastructure for years to come, ensuring that the platform is built to support diverse workloads and models.

title: The Future of Computing: Disaggregated Systems, AI Everywhere, and Agent Management
description: This transcript discusses the shift toward integrated, end-to-end data center strategies, the importance of disaggregated compute, and the growing necessity of managing AI agent consumption and behavior across all devices—from data centers to personal desktops.
summary:
The discussion emphasizes a fundamental shift in computing, moving away from isolated systems toward an integrated data center model where servers, hardware, networking, and power must work together. A key opportunity lies in co-designing CPUs and GPUs and addressing bottlenecks in the entire ecosystem.

The speaker highlights the growing demand for ultra-low latency inference, which necessitates disaggregated solutions (separating compute and memory bandwidth) to maximize performance. This led to a major partnership with Cerebrus and AMD to create a disaggregated solution that combines AMD CPUs, SRAM, and memory bandwidth.

Looking forward, the focus is on the pervasive nature of AI, where inference is no longer confined to data centers but will be distributed across edge devices, laptops, and desktops through "side-side computing" (agent swarms).

To manage this distributed environment, the solution involves a unified management stack, such as Cisco Cloud Control and Halo. This system provides full visibility into the entire estate (cloud, data center, devices), monitors token costs and agent behavior, and provides robust security guardrails. Ultimately, the goal is to ensure agents operate within defined token consumption guidelines, making the entire computing stack resilient, secure, and cost-effective.

title: Co-designing the Future: Hardware, Workloads, and Strategic Partnerships
description: This discussion focuses on the necessity of co-designing entire data center systems—integrating CPUs, GPUs, networking, and cooling—to meet future workload demands. It emphasizes the importance of strategic, multi-company partnerships to build scalable, reliable, and easily deployable hardware solutions.
summary: The conversation centers on the necessity of shifting the paradigm from single-component hardware design to holistic data center system co-design. The speaker stresses that solutions must integrate CPUs, GPUs, networking, storage, power distribution, and cooling systems into one cohesive unit, focusing on ease of use, deployability, and reliability. Technical specifications are highlighted, including advanced transistor technologies (2nm/3nm process) and the scale of current production hardware. A major theme is the strategic importance of partnership, emphasizing the need for open, heterogeneous collaborations to leverage the collective knowledge of various hardware and software teams. The partnership with Meta is cited as a prime example of successful co-design, where insights into future workloads drive the development of better chips and systems. Key collaborative focuses include optimizing power and cooling, ensuring full-stack solutions, and addressing safety and security, all to ensure that the entire apparatus can be deployed and managed with confidence.

title: AMD's AI Hardware Architecture: Triplet Innovation and Next-Generation Systems
description: This presentation details AMD's advanced AI hardware solutions, focusing on the Triplet Innovation, the high-performance EPYC Venice CPU, and the integrated MI455 accelerator. The talk emphasizes the strategic combination of hardware, software, and ecosystem partnerships to deliver the highest performance AI accelerators.
summary: The presentation introduced several key components of AMD's AI strategy. The speaker detailed the Triplet Innovation, which combines twelve compute and I/O triplets with 432 GB of memory, utilizing advanced 3D chipstack packaging to achieve the "highest performance AI accelerator in the industry." Hardware architecture was further explored by detailing the EPYC "Venice HF" CPU, which serves as the highest-performing chip for driving AI host nodes, featuring eight compute triplets (12 cores each at up to 5 GHz) and optimized I/O/memory bandwidth. The MI455 accelerator was shown to be mounted on the EAM, a comprehensive module that integrates the GPU, memory, power delivery, and system management. The talk highlighted the significant performance gains of the Helios system, noting 15% more compute, 50% more HBM4 memory capacity, and 50% more scale-out bandwidth. Strategically, the presentation stressed that hardware is only part of the story, emphasizing that software and platform development are crucial for building a developer-friendly ecosystem. The company discussed expanding unified memory capacity (up to 192GB) and reaching 300 billion parameters, focusing on creating rack-scale systems through deep partnerships with OEMs, and announcing a new Helios system annually.

title: The Venice CPU Family: Leading the Data Center for the Agentic Era
description: This segment introduces the Venice CPU family, highlighting its architectural versatility and performance leadership across diverse workloads—from GPU servers to dense agent sandboxes and general-purpose computing. Venice delivers superior performance-per-watt, making it the optimal choice for cloud, enterprise, and HPC applications.
summary:
The presentation establishes the Epic formula (performance, density, TCO) and introduces the Venice CPU family as the best server CPU in the world, designed specifically for the agentic era. Venice leverages the new Zen 6 core and a trilet architecture, offering a broad spectrum of chips (256-core for agentic sandboxes, smaller chips for enterprise/drone applications, and specialized models for HPC).

Venice excels across three primary server computing workloads: GPU servers (maximizing speed and feed), agent servers (achieving high density and agents per watt), and general-purpose servers (prioritizing efficiency and workload diversity).

Performance metrics demonstrate exceptional efficiency: Venice delivers more than twice the performance per watt for agent sandboxes and up to 3.3 times more performance per watt compared to leading ARM processors. It also delivers 2.2 times more performance at the socket level.

The product portfolio is flexible, spanning 8 to 13,156 cores across various power and I/O configurations, providing customers with the optimal solution for their specific needs. Future innovations include dedicated chips like Runo for AI host nodes and VeniceX, which utilizes 3D V-cache stacking for HPC.

Furthermore, the system integrates advanced software solutions, such as HyperLoom (for workload tuning and kernel optimization) and Rockum.AI

title: AMD's Strategy: Unifying AI Everywhere through Open Hardware and Agentic Software
description: This session outlines AMD's strategy to dominate the high-performance AI computing market by emphasizing an open hardware and software ecosystem, leveraging AI-assisted development tools like Rockum.AI to make AMD platforms accessible and powerful for all developers.
summary:
The speaker outlines AMD's mission to push the boundaries of high-performance and AI computing, focusing on deploying intelligence "everywhere"—from the cloud to edge devices—by differentiating itself through a market strategy built on open hardware and software. AMD projects significant market growth for its computing products and highlights that AI acts as a force multiplier, enabling faster deployment of workloads.

Key points discussed include:
*   **Market Vision:** The goal is to serve a massive, rapidly growing market (projected $2 trillion by 2030) by providing high-performance, adaptive computing solutions.
*   **Open Ecosystem:** AMD's strategy relies heavily on an open approach to both hardware and software (Rockum), which is crucial for servicing the broad AI market.
*   **AI Integration:** AI is transforming development, evidenced by the ability of AI to generate highly optimized GPU kernels, significantly improving performance and developer efficiency.
*   **Rockum.AI Platform:** The introduction of Rockum.AI, an agentic AI platform, is designed to bring AI-assisted GPU programming capabilities to developers, helping them understand and optimize AMD platforms.
*   **Hyperloom:** This AI-assisted optimization layer sits on top of the Rockum stack, making it easier for developers to achieve peak performance.
*   **Open Source Models:** AMD is driving the adoption of open-source models (like OTel 2.0) in the telecom sector to make hardware programming more accessible, allowing developers to use familiar frameworks and tools across the entire compute platform.

title: Advancements in AMD Instinct Hardware and AI Ecosystem
description: This segment reviews the performance leap of the MI455, details strategic partnerships, introduces new enterprise hardware like the MI350P, and outlines the future roadmap for the Instinct AI platform.
summary:
The segment highlights the technological foundation of the MI455 system, integrating high-performance components like the MI455 GPU, world's fastest CPU core, and Tensor DPUs. Performance metrics show that the MI455 delivers four times the throughput of the MI355 at lower concurrency and up to 34 times more throughput at the highest concurrency, offering up to 18 times more tokens per dollar. Power and bandwidth are key limiting factors.

Strategic efforts include landmark partnerships, such as deploying up to 6 gigawatts of AMD infrastructure, and a deep collaboration with Mellanox. The text emphasizes the importance of software optimization (VLLM, model recipes) and the role of rockum.ai in boosting training performance by 2.4 times.

New hardware introductions include the Instinct MI350P, designed to make LLM inference accessible in enterprise data centers without facility upgrades. The future roadmap points to subsequent generations like the MI500 (with larger HBM) and MI600 (with CDNA next), aiming for a generational leap in inference throughput and supporting sovereign AI initiatives.

title: Launch and Capabilities of the Helios AI Compute Rack
description: This session introduces Helios, the industry's highest performance AI roadmap and compute rack, highlighting its massive scale, advanced components, and exceptional performance. It details the collaboration between the hardware and software teams to optimize GVT class workloads.
summary: The speaker launched Helios, positioning it as the best AI rack in the world, designed to train and run the most demanding frontier models at massive scale. The Helios rack integrates Instinct, Epic, and Thinking chips, supports up to six Volcano Nicks, and utilizes an open Ultra Ethernet standard for networking, featuring 75 GPUs connected via UA Link over Ethernet. A single Helios rack boasts incredible specs, including over 18,000 CDNA5 TPU compute units, 4,600 Zynq PPU cores, and 31 TB of HBM4 memory. Helios is currently in full production with shipments scheduled to begin at the end of Q3 and ramp up in Q4. The collaboration with AMD engineers is focused on optimizing the software stack for GVT class workloads, with deployment expected at massive scale starting late this year and accelerating in 2027. The core innovation lies in combining the leader in performance and memory (Instinct/Helios) with the Cerebrus wafer scale engine, which provides five times the throughput while maintaining extraordinary speed for ultra-low latency inference.
